styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Gulangyu lanes, temples and the old town.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Seafood, street snacks and tea houses.

styles.label: Beach
styles.blurb: Island swims, causeways and sea views.

stays.why: Old-town streets, snack stalls and the ferry wharves nearby. Good base for first-timers.
Stay on the car-free island after day-trippers leave. Book ahead; luggage is carried by hand.
Quiet cafés and bars around the lake, close to the metro and downtown.
Near Nanputuo temple, the beach road and student food streets.

food: Try local seafood: oysters, crab and steamed fish, sold by weight at wet-market restaurants. Ask the price before ordering.
Snack streets around Zhongshan Road: peanut soup, oyster omelette and shacha noodles, mostly ¥10–30 a plate.
Gulangyu is known for fish balls and pineapple cakes; buy cakes as gifts near the ferry pier.
Fujian tea is big here. Sit in a tea house and try oolong; prices vary, so ask for the menu first.
Cheap and filling: noodle shops near Xiamen University. Expect ¥15–35 a bowl.
more_time: Add a day on Gulangyu: go early, walk the quiet back lanes and skip the busiest shopping streets.
Swap a city afternoon for the beach road and Nanputuo temple, then eat near the university.
Take a short trip out of town for a slower day; check timetables on the day.

recommend.why: Two nights cover Gulangyu, the old town and the beach road without rushing; add a night for a slower food day.

month_notes: Cool and fairly dry: highs near 18°C. Bring a jacket for evenings.
Similar to January, a little wetter. Light layers are enough.
Mild at 21°C with more rain days. Carry a small umbrella.
Warm and pleasant at 25°C; rain days rise.
Warm and humid, with frequent rain. Plan indoor backups.
Hot and very wet: about 20 rain days. Expect heavy showers.
Hottest month, highs near 33°C. Go out early or late.
Hot and wet again, with many rain days. Keep plans flexible.
Still hot at 31°C but rain eases. Good beach weather.
A sweet spot: warm, drier and comfortable. Book ahead.
Mild and dry at 25°C. Great for walking the old town.
Cooler at 20°C and dry. Pack a warm layer for nights.

climate_guide.summary: Subtropical and humid: mild, fairly dry winters and hot, wet summers with typhoon-season rain.

items.title: Best time: October to December
items.text: Warm days around 20–29°C and few rain days. Ideal for Gulangyu and the old town.

items.title: Wettest months: May to August
items.text: 15–20 rain days a month. Showers can be heavy; keep a rain jacket and a backup plan.

items.title: Hot summer
items.text: July and August peak near 32–33°C with warm nights. Sightsee early morning or after sunset.

items.title: Typhoon season
items.text: Summer and early autumn can bring storms. Check forecasts and ferry status on the day.

items.title: Mild winters
items.text: January and February sit around 11–19°C. A jacket is useful, especially near the water.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes, a rain layer, sunscreen and comfortable shoes for cobbled island lanes.

transit.best: Metro for the airport and main stops; ferries for Gulangyu.

modes.text: Lines 1–3 link the airport area, Xiamen North station and downtown. Signs are bilingual.
Cheap and frequent, but most route signs are Chinese only. BRT runs on elevated bus-only roads; use the T4 station for the airport.
Taxis start at ¥10. Ride-hailing apps like Didi work well.
Not needed for most trips; the metro, buses and ferries cover the main sights.
Best in the old town and on Gulangyu. Note bikes are banned on Gulangyu.
Ferries to Gulangyu leave from Dongdu Wharf for non-residents. Check times on the day.
Pay with the Alipay or WeChat transit mini-app, or an eKatong card.
